sections.heading: How to summarize a YouTube video
sections.body:
Paste a YouTube link into the tool and it writes a summary of the video. You do not have to watch the whole video first. You do not need an account, an app or a payment to try it.

1. Copy the link to the video. On a computer, open the video on youtube.com, click Share under the player, then click Copy.
2. Open [YouTube Video Summarizer](https://youtube-summarizer.lazur.app/) in your browser.
3. Paste the link into the box.
4. Choose a length: Key points, One paragraph or Detailed.
5. Run the summary, read it, then copy it with one click.

**The summary starts with a one-line title**, so you can tell at a glance which video it covers. Keep the link to the video handy, so you can go back to the original if a part of the summary needs a closer look.

sections.heading: Pick the length you need
sections.body:
Key points gives you a short list of the main ideas. Use it when you want to decide whether a video is worth your time, or when you need a quick set of notes.

One paragraph gives you a single block of text. Use it when you want something to paste into a message, a post or a document without editing it much.

Detailed gives the most room. Use it for lectures, interviews and tutorials, where the order of the steps and the names and numbers matter. A good routine is to start with Key points for a quick check, then run Detailed on the videos you plan to keep and use.

sections.heading: What the summary includes
sections.body:
The tool sends a fixed request for each summary. It asks for a one-line title first, then a summary in the length you chose. The request also asks for specifics, such as names, numbers and steps, when the video gives them. So a tutorial summary should list the steps in order, and a talk summary should name the main points the speaker makes.

Read the summary against the video before you act on anything in it, such as a price, a date, a setting or a medical or legal point. A summary is a shortcut to the video, not a replacement for it. It can leave out context, and it can get a detail wrong.

A summary is a shortcut, and shortcuts can miss things. The summary can leave out context, and it can get a detail wrong, so check any number, date, setting or claim you plan to use. The video is the source. The summary is there to point you to the right part of it.

A quick check works well. Read the summary, pick the one or two points that matter most to you, then jump to those parts in the video and confirm them. This takes a few minutes and is far faster than watching a long video from the start.
